prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A German glossary/reference table for very long compound terms, pairing each term with its abbreviation and a plain-language explanation.","reading":"Readers locate a row by scanning the full compound term or its short form, then read the explanation. Comparison happens mainly within a row, not across numeric columns.","groups":["Columns 1–2 form the identifier pair: the full compound and its abbreviation name the same entity and should stay adjacent and visually linked.","Column 3 is supporting prose, subordinate to the identifier pair and read after it."],"keep_intact":["Abbreviations in column 2, especially hyphenated forms such as Kfz-Haftpflicht","The 186px unbreakable word in column 3 if possible","Compound terms in column 1 where width allows; split only when necessary"],"may_wrap":["Explanation prose at word spaces","Long compound terms in column 1 when the chosen width cannot hold them","Column headers if needed"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [360, 122, 237] · table 720×906px · row heights [36, 153, 153, 153, 153, 106, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [220, 122, 377] · table 720×580px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 106, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [567, 122, 1112] · table 1802×255px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 1082px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
